title: Examination Based on the Beatitudes
description: A spiritual examination of conscience structured around Jesus's teachings on the Beatitudes from the Sermon on the Mount, guiding reflection on how we embody these teachings in daily life.

categories.title: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
categories.description: Being poor in spirit means recognizing our complete dependence on God and acknowledging that all good things come from Him.

items.text: Have I approached God with an attitude of entitlement rather than gratitude?
items.clarification: Being poor in spirit is about spiritual humility and dependence on God, not material poverty.

items.text: Have I attempted to control situations rather than surrendering to God's will?
Have I placed my trust in material possessions, talents, or achievements rather than in God?
Have I been self-sufficient to the point of excluding God from my decisions and actions?
Have I approached prayer with a humble heart, acknowledging my need for God's grace?
Have I sought status, recognition, or superiority over others?
Have I been grateful for God's blessings, recognizing them as gifts rather than entitlements or personal accomplishments?
Have I been willing to admit my mistakes, sins, and need for forgiveness?

categories.title: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
categories.description: This Beatitude encompasses sorrow for sin, empathy with others' suffering, and righteous grief over injustice in the world.

items.text: Have I been indifferent to my own sinfulness or failed to experience sorrow for my sins?
items.clarification: Mourning includes sorrow for sin, compassion for suffering, and righteous grief over injustice.

items.text: Have I been insensitive to the pain and suffering of others?
Have I been indifferent to injustice and evil in the world?
Have I avoided situations that might expose me to others' suffering?
Have I comforted those who are grieving, lonely, or troubled?
Have I been quick to offer platitudes rather than genuine compassion to those who suffer?
Have I prayed for those who are suffering or in distress?
Have I sought comfort only in worldly things rather than turning to God in times of sorrow?

categories.title: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.
categories.description: Meekness is not weakness, but strength under control. It means being gentle, patient, and humble in our dealings with others.

items.text: Have I insisted on my own way rather than being willing to yield to others?
items.clarification: Meekness is strength under control - power exercised with gentleness and patience.

items.text: Have I been harsh, domineering, or controlling in my relationships?
Have I responded to criticism or correction with defensiveness or anger rather than humility?
Have I sought to impose my views on others rather than respecting their freedom and dignity?
Have I been impatient or irritable rather than gentle and understanding?
Have I used my position, authority, or strength to dominate rather than to serve others?
Have I been willing to listen to others' perspectives with an open mind?
Have I practiced self-control in my words, actions, and reactions to others?

categories.title: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied.
categories.description: This Beatitude calls us to deeply desire holiness and justice, both in our own lives and in society.

items.text: Have I grown complacent in my spiritual life, satisfied with mediocrity rather than striving for holiness?
items.clarification: This hunger compels us to seek holiness in our own lives and justice in society.

items.text: Have I been more concerned with following rules than with growing in love for God and neighbor?
Have I been indifferent to injustice in my community or world?
Have I been reluctant to stand up for what is right when it was difficult or unpopular?
Have I worked and prayed for justice and the common good?
Have I sought to grow in virtue and holiness through prayer, sacraments, and spiritual practices?
Have I been content with superficial changes rather than deep conversion in areas of sin or weakness?
Have I been willing to sacrifice comfort, convenience, or status to pursue what is right?

categories.title: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
categories.description: Mercy involves compassion, forgiveness, and a willingness to help others in their need, as God has been merciful to us.

items.text: Have I been harsh or judgmental toward others while seeking leniency for myself?
items.clarification: Mercy is love's response to suffering - extending to others the compassion we've received from God.

items.text: Have I withheld forgiveness from those who have hurt me?
Have I been indifferent to the needs of the poor, the sick, or the marginalized?
Have I practiced the corporal and spiritual works of mercy?
Have I been quick to criticize and slow to understand others' struggles?
Have I given others the benefit of the doubt, or jumped to negative conclusions about their motives?
Have I prayed for those who have wronged me?
Have I shown compassion to those suffering, even when inconvenient or costly to me?

categories.title: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
categories.description: Purity of heart means integrity, sincerity, and singleness of purpose in seeking God above all else.

items.text: Have I been hypocritical, presenting one face to the world while harboring different thoughts and intentions?
items.clarification: Purity of heart is more than sexual purity - it encompasses integrity, sincerity, and single-minded devotion to God.

items.text: Have I been dishonest in my words or actions?
Have I harbored impure thoughts, images, or desires instead of guarding my heart and mind?
Have I sought to purify my intentions, doing good for God's glory rather than for recognition or reward?
Have I entertained media, conversations, or activities that have corrupted my mind or heart?
Have I been authentic and transparent in my relationships with others?
Have I maintained healthy boundaries to protect my heart and mind from corruption?
Have I practiced simplicity of intention, seeking to please God in all things?

categories.title: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
categories.description: Peacemaking goes beyond avoiding conflict to actively building harmony, reconciliation, and understanding in our relationships and communities.

items.text: Have I stirred up conflict, gossip, or division rather than promoting peace and unity?
items.clarification: Peacemaking is not merely avoiding conflict, but actively building harmony and reconciliation.

items.text: Have I been willing to take the first step toward reconciliation when relationships are strained?
Have I sought to understand others' perspectives or dismissed them without consideration?
Have I used my words to heal and unite rather than to wound and divide?
Have I prayed for peace and unity in my family, Church, community, and world?
Have I worked to resolve conflicts through dialogue and understanding rather than force or manipulation?
Have I cultivated peace in my own heart through prayer, forgiveness, and trust in God?
Have I been a voice of moderation and charity in polarized discussions or situations?

categories.title: Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
categories.description: This Beatitude calls us to remain faithful to Christ and his teachings even when it brings opposition, ridicule, or suffering.

items.text: Have I compromised my faith or values to avoid criticism or conflict?
items.clarification: This beatitude calls us to faithfulness even when it brings opposition or suffering.

items.text: Have I remained silent about my faith when I should have spoken up?
Have I supported fellow Christians who face persecution or discrimination?
Have I complained about minor inconveniences while ignoring the severe persecution others face for their faith?
Have I been willing to accept criticism or misunderstanding for adhering to Church teaching?
Have I prayed for those who oppose or persecute the Church?
Have I prayed for the strength to remain faithful to Christ regardless of the cost?
Have I responded to opposition with patience and love rather than anger or retaliation?
